Definition: a cord (of a tent); or the string (of a bow)
BiblicalUsage: The tabernacle had its cords and pins, and Isaiah tells Zion to lengthen her cords and strengthen her stakes. The word is the cord itself, and it holds the tent up and holds the bowstring taut.
TheologicalSignificance: I notice that Isaiah's cords are a promise of growth: lengthen them, spare not, because the tent is going to get bigger, and the God who stretches it will hold it.
